raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Batch `/derender` was decoding the stop token the engine had already left out of the text, so `stop` and `stop_token_ids` leaked and `stop_reason` stayed null. Fixes the batch half of #57052. Streaming `/derender` now returns 400 when the request carries stop strings, which is the direction on #47161.

## Claims

- A batch chat or completions derender drops the last token only when `finish_reason` is `stop` and that id is in the client's `stop_token_ids`, equals `tokenizer.eos_token_id`, or is in the model's `generation_config` `eos_token_id` list. `finish_reason=stop` alone does not drop a token. `include_stop_str_in_output` keeps it.
- The token check runs first. The stop-string check then runs on the text that remains, using the same `check_stop_strings` as the engine. A matched stop string wins. The space before the stop word stays.
- `stop_reason` is the matched string, or the token id. It stays empty for the primary EOS.
- Token ids on the generate response are not rewritten.
- Streaming `/derender` returns 400 if the chat or completion request carries stop strings.

## Validation

`pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stop.py` — 12 passed. The tests use a tiny in-memory tokenizer and do not need a GPU. They cover a stop string, keeping that string when asked, an ordinary last token left in place, a client `stop_token_ids` drop, a primary EOS drop with an empty `stop_reason`, a `generation_config` EOS drop, keeping the stop token when asked, the token check before the string scan, a `length` finish, and the completions stop string.

The live server tests in `test_derender.py` were not run. This machine cannot start `vllm serve`.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stop.py
```

## Details

The engine truncates `output_text` and then appends the stop token id back onto `token_ids`. ServingTokens ships those ids. Derender decoded the full list, so the stop word came back and `include_stop_str_in_output` did nothing.

Derender does not assume every `finish_reason=stop` input ends in a stop id. Round-trip fixtures encode real text and do not append one. Dropping that token broke `encode(derender(ids)) == ids`.

The batch pass recomputes the cut on the derender side because `GenerateResponseChoice` still has no `stop_reason` (#47313). Once that lands, derender can pass the field through instead of scanning.

The parser path scans text with special-token markers kept. The engine scans with `skip_special_tokens` applied, so a stop string that overlaps a marker can cut differently.

Streaming with no `chat_request` has no stop list to refuse, so that leak stays until `output_mode` (#56851).

Streaming is a 400, not a hold-back buffer. The engine-side fix is `output_mode` (#56851).

Logprobs are not trimmed to the shortened text.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

🚀

Thanks @pOpO1-9, this matches the design on #57052. I ran the branch locally: the 7 new tests pass and the existing derender unit and round-trip suites still pass (109 passed, 1 xfail).

One suggestion on the token rule. The engine skips the last token from text for any token-terminated stop, and it merges the model's generation-config stop tokens into `stop_token_ids` server-side (`SamplingParams.update_from_generation_config`), so the client's list is a subset. Checking membership misses EOS / end-of-turn tokens when `skip_special_tokens=False`. A simpler rule that matches the engine: `finish_reason == "stop"` and no stop string matched, then drop the last token (unless `include_stop_str_in_output`). No membership check needed.

Two things worth a sentence in the PR body: the parser path scans marker-preserving text while the engine scans with `skip_special_tokens` applied, so a stop string overlapping a marker can cut differently; and plain streaming with no `chat_request` can't be gated, so that leak stays until `output_mode`.

The live render → generate → derender comparison from #57052 would be the strongest validation once you have a machine with torch.

Thanks Shimi. That rule is cleaner, so I put it in.

If the finish reason is stop and no stop string matched, the last token comes out of the text. It stays when include_stop_str_in_output is set. A stop string still wins, and in that case the last token stays too.

I added your two notes to the description. The parser still reads text with the markers kept, so a stop string on a marker can cut differently from the engine. Streaming with no chat request still has nothing to refuse, so that leak waits on output_mode.

Thanks again for running the tests. I still cannot run the live render, generate, derender pass from this machine.

Thanks @shimib. You were right to walk that back.

The last token is dropped only when it is in the client's stop_token_ids, equals tokenizer.eos_token_id, or is in the generation_config eos list. stop_reason stays empty for the primary EOS, and is the token id otherwise. The token check runs first, then the stop string check on the text that is left.

The new unit tests pass, including the case where finish_reason is stop and the last token is ordinary text. I still cannot run the live server tests from this machine. Thank you for catching the round-trip.

Streaming `/derender` no longer returns 400 just because the request has stop strings.

Plain chat and completion streams hold the possible stop prefix in `stream_state` (`held_text`), the same `max(len(stop)) - 1` characters the engine holds. A matched stop string is cut, and later chunks emit nothing. A stop token is still dropped only when that id is a known stop.

Parser-configured chat streaming still returns 400. That path replays tokens through `parse_delta` and cannot hold a suffix back. The inline fix for that case remains `output_mode` on `/inference/v1/generate` (#56851, #58588).

The missing Signed-off-by on the previous commit is fixed. `pre-run-check` still requires a maintainer `ready` label before pre-commit runs.

Thanks Martin. Streaming is a 400 again.

`held_text`, `stop_fired`, `matched_stop_reason`, and `apply_streaming_stop` are gone, along with their tests.

Chat and completions both return 400 when the request carries stop strings, parser or not. The message points at `output_mode=text`. `derenderer.md` says streaming rejects stop.

A known stop token on the final chunk is still dropped. That check looks only at the current chunk, so it adds nothing to `stream_state`.

The unit tests for this pass. I still cannot run the live server from this machine.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @pOpO1-9.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

@pOpO1-9 cc @hickeyma

Once #60251 lands, generate reports the engine's `stop_reason` directly, so derender can use it instead of re-deriving the match. Suggested rule, which also sidesteps the fact that `None` from a new generate host and a missing field from an old one look identical after parsing:

1. If `choice.stop_reason is not None`, use it as-is and only apply the text/token trimming for that specific match.
2. If it is `None` and `finish_reason == "stop"`, run the local scan (stop token ids first, then stop strings, as this PR already does) and set `stop_reason` only when the scan actually matches.
3. Otherwise leave it `None` and don't trim.

Step 2 is a no-op exactly in the cases where a new host would have sent `None` anyway (EOS, `length`, abort), because there is nothing for the scan to match. So old and new hosts converge on the same answer, and derender never invents a `stop_reason` the engine didn't have. Whichever of the two PRs lands second rebases the five choice sites.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks @pOpO1-9, the batch fix looks good.

For streaming, can we go back to rejecting `stop` rather than holding text back? On #47161 we agreed (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161#issuecomment-5893681568, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161#issuecomment-5927631392, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161#issuecomment-5929874783) that streaming `/derender` returns a 400 for stop strings and points to `output_mode=text` (#56851) because the engine already does the hold-back. We also agreed to change `DerenderStreamState` only once, designing the #59590 logprob cursor and any future hold-back together. `held_text`, `stop_fired` and `matched_stop_reason` get ahead of that and once clients echo them back they're part of the wire format.

So could you:

- drop those three fields and `apply_streaming_stop` and its tests
- return the 400 for any streaming request with stop strings, chat or completions, parser or not (right now it's only chat with a parser)
- add a line to `derenderer.md` saying streaming rejects `stop`

Dropping a known stop token on the final chunk can stay if it doesn't need state. If it does, leave it out for now.

I was going to open a PR for the streaming 400 but yours covers it, so I'll leave it here. I'll review the batch part once streaming is updated.

Thanks @pOpO1-9, the streaming changes look good and its going in the right direction.

A few things that you might take a look at:

- It needs a rebase. #60073 moved parse/assembly out of _`derender_chat`, so the batch chat part will need some rework.
- `generation_eos_ids()` calls `try_get_generation_config()` on every choice and every stream chunk. That isn't cached and does a `GenerationConfig.from_pretrained` each time and in the stream path it runs on the event loop. Can you load it once in` __init__` like `InputProcessor` does? You can also use `self.model_config` directly instead of `getattr`.
- The stop string scan runs whatever the `finish_reason`. Can we only scan on `stop`? The engine also skips the check for the first `min_tokens`, so a note on that gap would help.
- The engine only treats EOS/generation config EOS as a stop when `ignore_eos` is off. Derender should check that too.
- The parser path now gets the trimmed ids as `model_output_token_ids`. The main server passes the full `output.token_ids`.
- `decode_with_stop` repeats the token stop logic in `strip_finished_stop_token`. Calling the helper keeps batch and streaming on one rule?
- Can the tests go in `test_derender.py` instead of a new file? `test_streaming_stop_strings_are_rejected_by_the_helper` and t`est_stop_helpers_match_the_coupled_rule`don't add much. The `held_text assert` seems to be left over and the module docstring still mentions streaming.
@pOpO1-9 Are you able to continue this PR?

files.patch:
@@ -97,6 +97,7 @@ The server keeps no state between calls. Everything the next call needs is in `s
 - **Send every chunk through, including the last ones.** The finish reason usually arrives with the final tokens. A chunk with a `finish_reason` and no tokens is accepted too and flushes any buffered tool call arguments. With `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`, generate ends with a usage only chunk (`choices: []`). Send it through derender like any other chunk to get the usage chunk for the response. `usage.prompt_tokens` is the request's `prompt_tokens` if set, otherwise the generate chunk's.
 - **Send the same context on every call.** `chat_request` and `prompt_token_ids` aren't kept between calls, so they go with every chunk including the usage chunk. Both are required when a tool or reasoning parser is configured. `prompt_token_ids` is the `token_ids` of the `GenerateRequest` returned by `/render`.
 - **Don't forward `[DONE]`.** It marks the end of the generate stream and isn't a chunk.
+- **`stop` strings are rejected.** A streaming chat or completions request that carries stop strings returns `400`. The engine holds that text back with `output_mode=text`. Batch `/derender` still applies stop strings. A known stop token on the final chunk is still dropped, and that check does not add fields to `stream_state`.
 
 Streaming derender resolves `logprobs` on the plain detokenization path, including `token_id:N` placeholders, same as the non-streaming endpoints (see [Streaming state and logprobs](#streaming-state-and-logprobs)). The parser path doesn't resolve them yet and drops them.

@@ -0,0 +1,268 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""Batch and streaming derender must hide stop text the coupled server hides."""
+
+import asyncio
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.completion.protocol import CompletionRequest
+from vllm.entrypoints.scale_out.token_in_token_out.protocol import (
+    GenerateResponse,
+    GenerateResponseChoice,
+    GenerateResponseStreamChoice,
+    GenerateStreamResponse,
+)
+from vllm.renderers.online_derenderer import (
+    OnlineDerenderer,
+    decode_with_stop,
+    normalize_stop_strings,
+    truncate_at_stop_string,
+)
+
+WORDS = {1: "one", 2: "two", 3: "three", 4: "number"}
+
+
+class _Tokenizer:
+    def __init__(self, eos_token_id=None):
+        self.eos_token_id = eos_token_id
+
+    def decode(self, token_ids, skip_special_tokens=True):
+        return " ".join(WORDS[token_id] for token_id in token_ids)
+
+
+def _derenderer(eos_token_id=None, generation_eos=None):
+    model_config = None
+    if generation_eos is not None:
+        model_config = SimpleNamespace(
+            try_get_generation_config=lambda: {"eos_token_id": generation_eos}
+        )
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        parser=None,
+        model_config=model_config,
+        renderer=SimpleNamespace(
+            get_tokenizer=lambda: _Tokenizer(eos_token_id=eos_token_id)
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _chat(token_ids, *, eos_token_id=None, generation_eos=None, **kwargs):
+    response = GenerateResponse(
+        request_id="chatcmpl-stop",
+        choices=[
+            GenerateResponseChoice(
+                index=0,
+                token_ids=token_ids,
+                finish_reason=kwargs.pop("finish_reason", "stop"),
+            )
+        ],
+    )
+    request = ChatCompletionRequest(
+        model="tiny",
+        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+    choices = OnlineDerenderer._derender_chat(
+        _derenderer(eos_token_id=eos_token_id, generation_eos=generation_eos),
+        response,
+        request,
+    )
+    return choices[0]
+
+
+def test_chat_stop_string_is_left_out_of_the_text():
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3], stop=["three"])
+    # Same cut as the engine: the stop word goes, the space before it stays.
+    assert choice.message.content == "one two "
+    assert choice.stop_reason == "three"
+
+
+def test_chat_keeps_the_stop_string_when_asked():
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3], stop=["three"], include_stop_str_in_output=True)
+    assert choice.message.content == "one two three"
+    assert choice.stop_reason == "three"
+
+
+def test_chat_keeps_the_last_token_when_it_is_not_a_stop_token():
+    # finish_reason stop alone is not enough. Round-trip fixtures encode
+    # real text and do not append a stop id.
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3])
+    assert choice.message.content == "one two three"
+    assert choice.stop_reason is None
+
+
+def test_chat_client_stop_token_drops_the_last_id():
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3], stop_token_ids=[3])
+    assert choice.message.content == "one two"
+    assert choice.stop_reason == 3
+
+
+def test_chat_primary_eos_drops_the_last_id_and_leaves_stop_reason_empty():
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3], eos_token_id=3)
+    assert choice.message.content == "one two"
+    assert choice.stop_reason is None
+
+
+def test_chat_generation_config_eos_drops_the_last_id():
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3], generation_eos=[3, 9])
+    assert choice.message.content == "one two"
+    assert choice.stop_reason == 3
+
+
+def test_chat_keeps_the_stop_token_when_asked():
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3], stop_token_ids=[3], include_stop_str_in_output=True)
+    assert choice.message.content == "one two three"
+    assert choice.stop_reason == 3
+
+
+def test_chat_token_stop_runs_before_the_string_scan():
+    # The engine drops the stop token, then looks for a stop string in what remains.
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3], eos_token_id=3, stop=["two"])
+    assert choice.message.content == "one "
+    assert choice.stop_reason == "two"
+
+
+def test_length_finish_keeps_the_last_token():
+    choice = _chat([1, 2, 3], finish_reason="length")
+    assert choice.message.content == "one two three"
+    assert choice.stop_reason is None
+
+
+def test_completion_stop_string_is_left_out_of_the_text():
+    response = GenerateResponse(
+        request_id="cmpl-stop",
+        choices=[
+            GenerateResponseChoice(
+                index=0,
+                token_ids=[1, 4],
+                finish_reason="stop",
+            )
+        ],
+    )
+    request = CompletionRequest(model="tiny", prompt="hi", stop=["number"])
+    choices, _, _ = OnlineDerenderer._derender_completion(
+        _derenderer(),
+        [response],
+        completion_request=request,
+    )
+    assert choices[0].text == "one "
+    assert choices[0].stop_reason == "number"
+
+
+def test_streaming_stop_strings_are_rejected_by_the_helper():
+    assert normalize_stop_strings(["three"]) == ["three"]
+    assert normalize_stop_strings([]) == []
+    assert normalize_stop_strings(None) == []
+
+
+def test_stop_helpers_match_the_coupled_rule():
+    text, ids, reason = decode_with_stop(
+        _Tokenizer(),
+        [1, 2, 3],
+        skip_special_tokens=True,
+        finish_reason="stop",
+        stop=None,
+        include_stop_str_in_output=False,
+        stop_token_ids=[3],
+    )
+    assert text == "one two"
+    assert ids == [1, 2]
+    assert reason == 3
+    kept, kept_ids, kept_reason = decode_with_stop(
+        _Tokenizer(),
+        [1, 2, 3],
+        skip_special_tokens=True,
+        finish_reason="stop",
+        stop=["three"],
+        include_stop_str_in_output=False,
+    )
+    assert kept == "one two "
+    assert kept_ids == [1, 2, 3]
+    assert kept_reason == "three"
+    text, reason = truncate_at_stop_string("one two three", ["three"], False)
+    assert text == "one two "
+    assert reason == "three"
+
+
+def _stream_chunk(token_ids, finish_reason=None):
+    return GenerateStreamResponse(
+        request_id="cmpl-stream-stop",
+        choices=[
+            GenerateResponseStreamChoice(
+                index=0,
+                token_ids=token_ids,
+                finish_reason=finish_reason,
+            )
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+def test_completion_stream_drops_a_known_stop_token_on_the_final_chunk():
+    seen: list[list[int]] = []
+
+    async def detok(tokenizer, delta_token_ids, stream_state, skip_special_tokens=True):
+        seen.append(list(delta_token_ids))
+        text = " ".join(WORDS[token_id] for token_id in delta_token_ids)
+        return text, stream_state
+
+    derenderer = SimpleNamespace(
+        _detokenize_delta_async=detok,
+        renderer=SimpleNamespace(get_tokenizer=lambda: _Tokenizer(eos_token_id=9)),
+        model_config=None,
+    )
+    request = CompletionRequest(model="tiny", prompt="hi", stop_token_ids=[3])
+
+    async def run():
+        first, stream_state = await OnlineDerenderer.derender_completion_stream(
+            derenderer,
+            "tiny",
+            _stream_chunk([1, 2]),
+            completion_request=request,
+        )
+        second, stream_state = await OnlineDerenderer.derender_completion_stream(
+            derenderer,
+            "tiny",
+            _stream_chunk([3], finish_reason="stop"),
+            state=stream_state,
+            completion_request=request,
+        )
+        return first, second, stream_state
+
+    first, second, stream_state = asyncio.run(run())
+    assert first.choices[0].text == "one two"
+    assert first.choices[0].stop_reason is None
+    assert second.choices[0].text == ""
+    assert second.choices[0].stop_reason == 3
+    assert not hasattr(stream_state, "held_text")
+    assert seen == [[1, 2], []]
+
+
+def test_completion_stream_keeps_the_stop_token_when_asked():
+    async def detok(tokenizer, delta_token_ids, stream_state, skip_special_tokens=True):
+        text = " ".join(WORDS[token_id] for token_id in delta_token_ids)
+        return text, stream_state
+
+    derenderer = SimpleNamespace(
+        _detokenize_delta_async=detok,
+        renderer=SimpleNamespace(get_tokenizer=lambda: _Tokenizer()),
+        model_config=None,
+    )
+    request = CompletionRequest(
+        model="tiny",

Thanks @pOpO1-9, this matches the design on #57052. I ran the branch locally: the 7 new tests pass and the existing derender unit and round-trip suites still pass (109 passed, 1 xfail).

One suggestion on the token rule. The engine skips the last token from text for any token-terminated stop, and it merges the model's generation-config stop tokens into `stop_token_ids` server-side (`SamplingParams.update_from_generation_config`), so the client's list is a subset. Checking membership misses EOS / end-of-turn tokens when `skip_special_tokens=False`. A simpler rule that matches the engine: `finish_reason == "stop"` and no stop string matched, then drop the last token (unless `include_stop_str_in_output`). No membership check needed.

Two things worth a sentence in the PR body: the parser path scans marker-preserving text while the engine scans with `skip_special_tokens` applied, so a stop string overlapping a marker can cut differently; and plain streaming with no `chat_request` can't be gated, so that leak stays until `output_mode`.

The live render → generate → derender comparison from #57052 would be the strongest validation once you have a machine with torch.

Thanks Shimi. That rule is cleaner, so I put it in.

If the finish reason is stop and no stop string matched, the last token comes out of the text. It stays when include_stop_str_in_output is set. A stop string still wins, and in that case the last token stays too.

I added your two notes to the description. The parser still reads text with the markers kept, so a stop string on a marker can cut differently from the engine. Streaming with no chat request still has nothing to refuse, so that leak waits on output_mode.

Thanks again for running the tests. I still cannot run the live render, generate, derender pass from this machine.

Thanks @shimib. You were right to walk that back.

The last token is dropped only when it is in the client's stop_token_ids, equals tokenizer.eos_token_id, or is in the generation_config eos list. stop_reason stays empty for the primary EOS, and is the token id otherwise. The token check runs first, then the stop string check on the text that is left.

The new unit tests pass, including the case where finish_reason is stop and the last token is ordinary text. I still cannot run the live server tests from this machine. Thank you for catching the round-trip.

Streaming `/derender` no longer returns 400 just because the request has stop strings.

Plain chat and completion streams hold the possible stop prefix in `stream_state` (`held_text`), the same `max(len(stop)) - 1` characters the engine holds. A matched stop string is cut, and later chunks emit nothing. A stop token is still dropped only when that id is a known stop.

Parser-configured chat streaming still returns 400. That path replays tokens through `parse_delta` and cannot hold a suffix back. The inline fix for that case remains `output_mode` on `/inference/v1/generate` (#56851, #58588).

The missing Signed-off-by on the previous commit is fixed. `pre-run-check` still requires a maintainer `ready` label before pre-commit runs.

Thanks Martin. Streaming is a 400 again.

`held_text`, `stop_fired`, `matched_stop_reason`, and `apply_streaming_stop` are gone, along with their tests.

Chat and completions both return 400 when the request carries stop strings, parser or not. The message points at `output_mode=text`. `derenderer.md` says streaming rejects stop.

A known stop token on the final chunk is still dropped. That check looks only at the current chunk, so it adds nothing to `stream_state`.

@pOpO1-9 cc @hickeyma

Once #60251 lands, generate reports the engine's `stop_reason` directly, so derender can use it instead of re-deriving the match. Suggested rule, which also sidesteps the fact that `None` from a new generate host and a missing field from an old one look identical after parsing:

1. If `choice.stop_reason is not None`, use it as-is and only apply the text/token trimming for that specific match.
2. If it is `None` and `finish_reason == "stop"`, run the local scan (stop token ids first, then stop strings, as this PR already does) and set `stop_reason` only when the scan actually matches.
3. Otherwise leave it `None` and don't trim.

Step 2 is a no-op exactly in the cases where a new host would have sent `None` anyway (EOS, `length`, abort), because there is nothing for the scan to match. So old and new hosts converge on the same answer, and derender never invents a `stop_reason` the engine didn't have. Whichever of the two PRs lands second rebases the five choice sites.
